workflow: GSD background agents that die with transient API errors (socket closed, stream timeout) often auto-recover and complete — always check if the output file was written before respawning to avoid duplicate overwrites
When respawning a failed agent, call TaskStop on the duplicate immediately after the original completes; the original may finish before the respawn does
A process restart kills all in-flight background agents mid-task; their output files should be inspected to determine what partial work (if any) landed
The gsd-tools commit helper can report commit_failed as a false negative when lint-staged's spinner output is misread as an error; verify via git log
markdownlint MD040 (code fences missing language tag) is enforced by lint-staged at commit time — worth checking before committing generated docs

Verification agents doing deeper re-scans can surface new findings not caught in the initial pass (e.g. FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION line 22 was missed in round 1); run re-verification even on 'passing' docs in the fix loop
The GSD fix loop cap is 2 iterations; residual failures after cap exhaustion require manual edits using verifier-supplied corrected values

friction: Two Wave 1 agents (ARCHITECTURE and CONFIGURATION) died with transient API errors (socket closed, stream idle timeout) after consuming 55 and 74 tool calls respectively, requiring respawns and careful deduplication when the originals later auto-recovered
Process restart mid-iteration-2 killed all 5 fix agents simultaneously; their edits had not landed, requiring manual application of remaining corrections

METADATA_SCHEMAS.md required the most fix iterations — 16 stale package paths plus Rust line ranges; the iteration-2 fixer introduced new wrong file references (file.rs instead of folder.rs) that had to be corrected by hand
TaskStop failed silently on the two orphaned respawn agents because they had already died with the old process before the stop command reached them

The model_profile: adaptive config warning was emitted as 'unknown config key' on every gsd-tools invocation throughout the entire session but only surfaced as a named warning in the health check at the end
